newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilder rates retreat from highs.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilder rates retreat from highs.

text.p: Dutch call money rates retreated from Wednesday's highs during Thursday's session while the guilder held steady against the mark.
Call money started trading at the highs reached on Wednesday, changing hands at 3.50 percent, before easing back to bid at 3.12/3.18 percent in the early afternoon.
Other money market rates were broadly unchanged and the month-end kept market players busy.
One dealer said call had coasted higher on Wednesday on an 800 million guilder deal between the Dutch central bank and a European counterpart which caused a liquidity shortage.
A central bank official confirmed the bank had bought guilders from other central banks but declined to comment on the amount or the identity of the counterparties.

The amount of money Dutch banks held with the central bank under the cash reserve arrangement declined by 730 million guilders between Tuesday and Wednesday, the central bank's DNBG page on Reuters shows.

"We will give the market extra money through an ample allocation under the new special advances pact tomorrow, in order to make up for the unplanned eating into the cash reserve," the central bank official said.
One dealer said the transactions might well have been intended to support the guilder, which had reached a four-year low against the German mark on Tuesday.
"Otherwise, these other central banks might have put those guilders on the money market," he said.

The weakening of the guilder against the mark to below its central parity rate under the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) of 1.12673 guilders had fuelled speculation about a hike in the special advances rate this afternoon.
But the guilder has since firmed to 1.1263 at 1125 GMT.
Money market players and analysts no longer expect the central bank to move on the rate.
A poll of 10 bank economists conducted by Reuters this morning found that none of them expected the central bank to change the special advances rate.
Dealers said end-of-month business pumped up volumes today. "At least 10 to 11 billion guilders in taxes has to be paid today," one dealer said.
